instruction: I am in the process of hiring for Graphic Designer role for my company. I have selected candidates and prepared acceptance/rejection email templates and the offer letter template. You can find it all in "~/documents/work/hiring" in my file system. The candidates have applied to this position by emailing me over the last 3 weeks. Please reply to them individually following the appropriate decision templates.
notes: Two apps (file_system, gmail) plus supervisor. The agent lists ~/documents/work/hiring, reads the selected-candidates list, both email templates and the offer letter template, searches the inbox for Graphic Designer applications from the last 3 weeks (min_created_at = 2023-04-27T00:00:00 given current date 2023-05-18), opens each thread to get the candidate's email id, creates a personalized offer letter file (path containing 'offer_letter'; no existing file is overwritten or deleted) for each selected candidate, and replies with reply_to_email (so the subject becomes 'Re: ...' and the recipient defaults to the sender). A single gmail-reply-to-email action covers both decisions: the attachment parameter is bound to the created offer letter file for selected candidates and to the placeholder no-attachment (meaning attachment_file_paths/file_system_access_token are omitted) for rejected candidates. Tokens are tied to their app via token-of so logins cannot be confused. The number and identity of candidates are only known at runtime; the problem uses representative placeholders (2 selected, 2 rejected) and the create_file/reply steps repeat per actual candidate. Candidate decisions, thread/email ownership, template choice and filled bodies are static world facts in :init gated by knowledge predicates (directory-listed, file-read, applications-searched, thread-read). supervisor-complete-task takes the candidate records as non-API parameters with equality constraints so its precondition is exactly the lifted goal conjunction; it is called with no answer.
